title: Generative AI voting: fair collective choice is resilient to LLM biases and inconsistencies

bias_targets.methodology: Mapping self-reported personal traits to cognitive heuristics (e.g., time-discounting, optimism, surrogation, conformity, affect, altruism, and egotism) and using SHAP and LIME feature importance to evaluate how these biases impact the consistency and transitivity of AI-generated voting choices compared to humans.

Analyzing how political ideology, beliefs, and interests influence the accuracy of AI-generated ballots compared to actual human voters in real-world participatory budgeting and US national elections.

Evaluating human-AI choice consistency across demographic traits (such as race, gender, age, education, citizenship, and household size) as manifestations of unconscious bias, and assessing prediction disparities across these groups.
